reason: The sources provide sufficient details to support a 45-second story with well-supported claims.
story: Deep in the constellation Lynx, astronomers found a cosmic titan that shatters our expectations of galactic scale. Named Alcyoneus after a mythological Greek giant, this radio galaxy spans an astonishing 16 million light-years across. If you lined up one hundred Milky Ways end to end, they would barely match the length of its colossal plasma plumes. Discovered in 2022 by a team led by Martijn Oei using the LOFAR telescope network, Alcyoneus emits twin jet streams powered by a supermassive black hole at its core. Yet, the real mystery isn't its gargantuan size—it's how it got so big. Despite its record-breaking radio lobes, Alcyoneus is otherwise a surprisingly ordinary elliptical galaxy, with a normal stellar mass and black hole size. Scientists suspect its low-density cosmic web environment might be the secret, letting its jets stretch to unprecedented proportions without resistance.
angle: Alcyoneus is a 16-million-light-year-wide cosmic giant whose massive radio plumes stretch the length of 100 Milky Ways, yet its central galaxy is completely ordinary.

claims.claim: Alcyoneus is a radio galaxy located approximately 3 billion to 3.5 billion light-years from Earth.
Its lobed structures span 5 megaparsecs, or about 16 million light-years across.
The galaxy's length is equivalent to more than 100 Milky Ways laid end to end.
The discovery was reported in February 2022 by a team of astronomers led by Martijn Oei.
The discovery was made using data from the Low-Frequency Array (LOFAR) network of radio telescopes.
Alcyoneus is located in the northern constellation of Lynx.
The galaxy was named after the giant Alcyoneus from Greek mythology.
The central host galaxy has a stellar mass of approximately 240 billion solar masses.
The central supermassive black hole has an estimated mass of around 390 to 400 million solar masses.
Alcyoneus is a relatively quiescent elliptical galaxy with a star formation rate of only 0.016 solar masses per year.
At the time of its announcement, it was described by its discoverers as the largest known structure of galactic origin.
The findings were accepted for publication in the journal Astronomy & Astrophysics.

disputed: Sources vary slightly on the exact distance to Earth (stating either roughly 3 billion or 3.5 billion light-years) and precise property measurements like exact megaparsecs (4.99 vs 5.04 Mpc). A script should use general phrasing like 'about 3 billion light-years away' and '16 million light-years wide'.
